raw_prompt: Implement password reset session invalidation that blacklists active refresh tokens across all clusters.

cumulative_requirements.title: Password Reset Session Invalidation
cumulative_requirements.description: Trigger invalidation of active user sessions upon a successful password reset event.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt requirement: 'Implement password reset session invalidation'.

cumulative_requirements.title: Refresh Token Blacklisting Across Clusters
cumulative_requirements.description: Blacklist active refresh tokens across all deployment clusters upon session invalidation triggered by password reset.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt requirement: 'blacklists active refresh tokens across all clusters'.

cumulative_requirements.title: Distributed Token Revocation Propagation
cumulative_requirements.description: Revocation lists or states must synchronize or be queryable across all independent clusters with bounded propagation latency.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Why 1: Without cross-cluster synchronization, a refresh token invalidated in Cluster A could still be accepted in Cluster B. Why 2: A distributed caching layer, centralized database check, or pub/sub revocation broadcast mechanism is required to enforce global invalidation. Why 3: Revocation status must achieve eventual consistency across all compute boundaries within an acceptable security window.

cumulative_requirements.title: Token Identifier Uniqueness and Extraction
cumulative_requirements.description: Refresh tokens or their unique cryptographic identifiers (JTI) must be extractable and matched against the revocation blacklist during authentication verification.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Why 1: Blacklisting entire tokens requires a reliable identifier to prevent unbounded memory usage or imprecise matching. Why 2: The authentication middleware must parse the token identifier and perform an O(1) or O(log N) lookup against the blacklist store. Why 3: Any validly signed refresh token whose identifier appears in the blacklist must be rejected unconditionally.

cumulative_requirements.title: Token Storage Mechanism and Protocol Standards
cumulative_requirements.description: The specific data store (e.g., Redis cluster, SQL database) and token format standards (e.g., JWT, opaque tokens) are unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify the underlying datastore topology or whether tokens are structured JWTs or opaque references.

cumulative_requirements.title: Cross-Cluster Sync Latency and Consistency Model
cumulative_requirements.description: The exact acceptable replication lag or consistency model (e.g., strong vs. eventual consistency) for multi-cluster sync is unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: The prompt mandates cross-cluster blacklisting but does not define maximum allowable propagation latency SLA.

cumulative_requirements.title: Idempotent Blacklist Insertion and Storage Hygiene
cumulative_requirements.description: Blacklist state insertions for refresh token JTIs must be idempotent to prevent race conditions during concurrent reset events or duplicate propagation deliveries, and must incorporate token-lifetime-bound Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration.
cumulative_requirements.provenance: Distributed Systems Data Integrity & Security Standards
cumulative_requirements.justification: Step 1: If multiple concurrent password reset requests or redelivered synchronization events occur, non-idempotent insertions can cause distributed lock contention or state corruption. Step 2: Without automatic TTL expiration aligned with the token's remaining validity, the blacklist storage would grow unbounded, causing memory/storage exhaustion. Step 3: Therefore, enforcing idempotent writes and bounded TTL expiry preserves data integrity and prevents resource degradation across all clusters.

cumulative_requirements.title: Partition-Tolerant Fail-Closed Access Gate
cumulative_requirements.description: If a cluster loses connectivity to the cross-cluster revocation synchronization layer or blacklist store, authentication verification must enforce a fail-closed posture for refresh token validation to prevent revoked token reuse during network partitions.
cumulative_requirements.provenance: Zero Trust Security Architecture & Distributed Failure Modes
cumulative_requirements.justification: Step 1: During a network partition, isolated clusters cannot verify if a refresh token has been blacklisted due to a recent password reset. Step 2: A fail-open approach would allow compromised, pre-reset refresh tokens to successfully authenticate users during outages, defeating the security guarantee of the password reset. Step 3: Therefore, a fail-closed authorization gate must block refresh token validation when revocation status cannot be definitively confirmed.

cumulative_requirements.title: Crash Recovery and Blacklist State Rehydration
cumulative_requirements.description: Upon node restart or cluster crash recovery, the local revocation store or proxy cache must rehydrate blacklist state or block validation until synchronization with the authoritative global blacklist store is fully re-established.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Operational lifecycle boundary requiring secure behavior after a crash or power loss event to prevent temporary revocation bypass.

cumulative_requirements.title: Cryptographic Algorithm and Hashing Standard for Blacklisted Tokens
cumulative_requirements.description: The specific cryptographic hashing algorithm (e.g., SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256) used to store or index revoked token identifiers (JTIs) in the blacklist store is unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Underspecified architectural technology choice concerning cryptographic implementation details for token identity storage.

cumulative_requirements.title: Identity Provider and Directory Integration Protocol
cumulative_requirements.description: The upstream Identity Provider (IdP), directory service, or user store protocol (e.g., OIDC, SAML, LDAP) interfacing with the password reset trigger is unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Underspecified upstream dependency and integration boundary for capturing password reset events.
